items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication boundaries, least privilege, secrets handling, container isolation, release provenance and approvals, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not establish complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 35 pass, 14 fail, and 10 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of compromise. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, and medium for bounded growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; allow only bounded reversible growth within existing consent, disclosure, data-handling, and claims boundaries; continue the existing read-only evidence matrix; authorize no credential access, permission or configuration changes, dependency additions, deployments, requeues, external outreach, or security-sensitive release until material controls are evidenced and owner review is complete.

Retain the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix covering authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Record dated evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.
